The existing make gfx-preset-overwrite-check runtime test verifies prompt, cancel and confirmed file changes

GxProofs.GfxLightShadowSlots.justification: Light-slot reuse and shared point-shadow ownership affect renderer state and shadow validity.
GxProofs.GfxLightShadowSlots.scope: Two-slot lifecycle and lazy demand scan plus 64-slot/384-layer arithmetic: valid-pair non-aliasing and guarded overflow skip with a source-pinned 128-slot light heap
gaps: The model represents source failure cleanup as a reset; it does not establish that GPU failure occurs or that a later allocation succeeds. GPU resource validity, depth rendering and sampling are not proved
The source guard pins the configured heap maximum and generic growth checks; it is not a formal execution proof of the C heap or allocation success

Runtime checks remain separate: make gfx-art-light-check covers authored-art removal/reuse ownership, make gfx-light-check covers slot behavior, and make gfx-shadow-check covers point-shadow images plus the slot-63/64 allocation boundary

GxProofsGfx.Renderer.LightAttenuation.justification: Exact-real attenuation cutoff model covers quadratic, linear-only, zero-rate and conservative unbounded policies.
GxProofsGfx.Renderer.LightAttenuation.scope: Exact-real reciprocal attenuation monotonicity, quadratic and linear-only brightness epsilon roots, and a radius-policy model distinguishing zero, finite, and unbounded cutoffs
gaps: The Lean model uses exact real coefficients and does not model IEEE F32 non-finite values, C projection, GLSL, a driver, or GPU execution
Negative-coefficient and unbounded policy branches are modeled, but no general C-to-Lean proof establishes conservative execution for arbitrary malformed light data
Runtime Phong/PBR captures with smooth/flat normals and GL43 grid parity measure only the tested scene and inputs, not all materials, angles or coefficient ranges
The current Gouraud vertex path evaluates ambient/sun terms only; point-light attenuation and clustered culling are not covered there

GxMath.Sky.justification: Cartesian sky-frame conversions couple observer angles, axis signs and handedness; inverse/norm/orientation proofs and source witnesses protect convention-sensitive sky placement.

GxMath.Coordinates.justification: Coordinate conversions feed geometric tooling and sky placement; branch-aware inverse/radius contracts protect axis order and inclination semantics without claiming IEEE or singular-origin behavior.

GxMath.Units.justification: Basic length and temperature conversions are bounded numeric utilities; bidirectional identities and source constants matter more than broad engine state.

GxMath.Calculus.justification: Finite differences and quadrature support numeric utilities; polynomial and positive-even-step Simpson integral identities pin formulas while preserving convergence, tolerance and IEEE limits.
